title: Cascade Metrics — Embeddings + Rerank Hosted API Lab
summary: Hands-on hosted API walkthrough focusing on embeddings + rerank for product search. Covered model choices, embeddings dimensionality, top_k vs rerank tradeoffs, prefix caching and latency SLOs, and enterprise security (SSO, KMS, audit logs). Agreed to run a 2-week pilot: Redwood to provide benchmark checklist and sample prompt set; Cascade to provide a 50k doc subset and query log. Next steps: pilot kickoff, pricing worksheet, security pack share.
topics: Rerank endpoint vs client-side top_k scoring
Latency vs cost tradeoffs (batching, top_k, rerank depth)
Model selection for vector quality vs token cost
Security/compliance: SSO, SOC2, KMS, VPC options
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-04 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~54m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Samira (Cascade Head of Search), Ben (Cascade ML), Riley (CTO)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intro — I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer. we'll do a short overview and then go hands-on with the embeddings + rerank hosted endpoints.
[00:18] Samira: thanks Jordan. excited. we've got a search problem where product results feel noisy for long-tail queries, and our current embed + faiss pipeline doesn't always capture intent.
[00:28] Ben: yes and we have about 3 million SKUs, but for the pilot we'll share a 50k slice and query logs.
[00:36] Priya: great. quick agenda: 1) API shape for embeddings, 2) ingestion and dimensionality considerations, 3) how rerank endpoint fits into a pipeline vs doing top_k client-side, 4) perf/cost knobs in Redwood Optimize and Console.
[00:52] Riley: quick logistics question — we are very strict on encryption keys, KMS, and need audit logs. is that in the hosted plan or does that push us to private?
[01:03] Jordan: good Q. Hosted supports customer-managed KMS for enterprise plans and audit logs + SSO, SOC2 compliance artifacts. for strict network isolation you'd look at Private but often customers start hosted with CMK. we'll share the security pack after.
[01:18] Samira: cool. show us the API.
[01:23] Priya: switching to demo — sample call: POST /v1/embeddings with text array, choose a model (we'll demo a 1k-dim and a 768-dim). response is vector per input, JSON with token counts. note: embeddings are deterministic unless you pass stochastic params, so reproducible.
[01:44] Ben: are these the new quantized variants? we worry about small differences in cosine similarity when quantizing.
[01:50] Priya: Redwood curates model variants. quantized variants are fine for retrieval at high recall, but for tiny margin-sensitive rerank scores we often recommend a float16 variant for the final rerank. also you can use an asymmetric quantization for indexing (faiss, milvus), and call rerank on short-listed candidates with full-precision model.
[02:12] Jordan: this is where rerank fits — do cheap vector index to get top_k, then call Redwood rerank endpoint with the query + candidates for higher-fidelity scoring.
[02:22] [02:22] Samira: okay, demo the rerank payload.
[02:25] Priya: sure. POST /v1/rerank with query, list of candidate ids and contexts. you can ask for a score (0-1) or structured reason. sample output shown. note the request supports streaming so you can surface progressive scores in your app.
[02:40] Ben: what's the typical latency for rerank of 10 candidates on hosted?
[02:44] Priya: for our curated float16 model, median p50 is ~75-120ms per request for 10 candidates on hosted in us-west region, p95 ~250-400ms depending on sequence length. we can push lower with batching and prefix caching if queries repeat.
[03:04] Riley: 250-400ms p95... for product search that can be tight. how do we keep p95 below 300?
[03:11] Priya: options — reduce rerank depth (top_k 5 instead of 20), use a faster model variant (smaller embedding/rerank model), or enable auto-batching with low max_wait_ms to amortize cost. Redwood Optimize will recommend settings per your query distribution. also fallback policies can serve cheaper variants when load spikes.
[03:33] Samira: what's the unit cost model? are we billed per token for rerank? per candidate?
[03:38] Jordan: hosted pricing is per-token for generative/rerank calls, and per-embedding unit for embeddings. we provide cost estimates in the Console; Redwood Optimize simulates per-query cost given top_k, model, and batch sizes. we'll send a pricing worksheet.
[03:53] Ben: for indexing we use faiss on our side; are there connectors for vector DBs?
[03:58] Priya: yes — Redwood plays nicely with Faiss, Milvus, Pinecone. you export embeddings and index however you like. many customers use Redwood-hosted embeddings and then their own vector DB for retrieval, then call Redwood rerank. Others use Redwood pipelines to host both.
[04:12] Jordan: quick live example: I have a sample dataset of product descriptions. I'll run a query, show top 50 by dot-product then call rerank on top 10 to show the difference.
[04:22] [04:22] (typing sounds)
[04:35] Priya: running embeddings for the corpus now — note the API returns vector and meta: model name, dims, returned_at. sometimes transcripts show odd model names — we saw a weird 'redwnd-emb-1' in beta logs, but ignore that, it's prototype.
[04:52] Samira: hah, yeah those auto-names confuse folks.
[05:00] Priya: okay here's top_k 50 results — you can see surface-level matches. after rerank, results reorder to prioritize intent and attributes like "size availability".
[05:15] Ben: wow the rerank pulled up items with phrase matches even though embedding dot score was lower.
[05:20] Priya: rerank uses cross-encoder-style scoring which looks at query+candidate together so phrase-level relevance helps.
[05:28] Riley: can rerank also output structured signals, like reason tags? e.g., "matches color" or "size mismatch"?
[05:33] Priya: yes we have structured output; you can request explainability tokens. note that increases latency slightly because the model outputs more tokens, but it helps downstream features and quality monitoring. Redwood Console stores these reasoning tags for quality dashboards.
[05:52] Samira: we need to monitor precision/recall for top1 within our query sets. does the Console let us create eval sets?
[05:58] Jordan: yes — Console has an Evals integration. you can upload labeled queries and Console will score model variants, show regressions, and tie to alerts. Redwood Optimize can suggest switching model for rerank if regression is detected.
[06:10] Ben: question about rate limits and burst behavior — we have periodic spikes from promotions. how does Redwood handle bursts without losing requests?
[06:18] Priya: hosted has burst capacity tiers; for sustained spikes you may want Dedicated. there's also graceful degradation: fallback to cheaper model variants or reduce rerank depth so you keep p99 SLOs. we can set routing policies per API key.
[06:33] Riley: great. from a security perspective, what logs do you provide for audit?
[06:38] Jordan: full request logs (metadata only), per-token usage, per-route latency traces, and we can integrate with your SIEM via syslog/S3 export. for enterprise we support SAML SSO, SCIM, RBAC roles.
[06:51] Samira: does hosted keep any query text? data retention policy?
[06:55] Jordan: hosted offers configurable retention windows; for enterprise we can disable retention or set customer-controlled retention. we also support end-to-end encryption with customer-managed keys for stored artifacts.
[07:08] Ben: ok policy looks fine. can we run an A/B using canary rollouts? we want to test rerank on 10% traffic.
[07:15] Priya: yes Console supports canary rollouts and A/B with automatic fallback if quality drops. you can route by header, api_key, or percentage.
[07:27] Samira: let's talk metrics for the pilot — our success criteria: +8% top1 relevance on labeled set, p95 latency < 350ms, cost per query <$0.05. doable?
[07:38] Priya: those are reasonable. pilot plan we suggest: 2 weeks, run on 50k doc slice, label 5k queries, baseline + Redwood pipeline. We'll provide prompts & eval harness.
[07:51] Jordan: action: we'll populate the pilot checklist and share pricing.
[07:55] Samira: cool. any red flags on our side? Ben: we have on-prem data policy for source docs — can we keep embeddings generation on our infra?
[08:05] Priya: yes — you can host embeddings generation (private) and still call Redwood rerank hosted, or call Redwood embeddings and index in your infra. hybrid is supported. if you need fully air-gapped inference, that's Private deployment.
[08:18] Riley: we've seen minor inconsistencies across model versions causing rerank drift. how do you handle model rollouts?
[08:24] Priya: we support pinned model versions and transparent changelogs. Console warns on breaking changes and Evals tracks regressions. you can pin to a version until you validate.
[08:35] [08:35] Samira: who do we contact to start the pilot?
[08:38] Jordan: me — I'll send the pilot doc and pricing worksheet. Priya will own the benchmarking checklist and will help run the first batch.
[08:46] Ben: any recommended default top_k and rerank depth?
[08:49] Priya: start with top_k 50, rerank depth 10, then iterate. For long-tail heavy catalogs we sometimes do top_k 100 with cheap model then rerank 10 with heavier model. Redwood Optimize will run simulation on your query histogram and recommend.
[09:05] Samira: about vector dims — is 768 enough? we currently use 512.
[09:09] Priya: 768 is a good sweet spot for semantic nuance on commerce; 1024 helps but costs more. 512 may under-encode attributes. We can test both in pilot and see eval scores.
[09:22] Riley: do you provide sample notebooks for integrating with Faiss?
[09:26] Jordan: yes — we'll include a repo with code snippets for faiss indexing, Milvus connector, and a sample rerank loop.
[09:34] Ben: can rerank read product attributes like stock, price to bias result? we sometimes want to boost in-stock or promo items.
[09:40] Priya: absolutely — you can pass structured payloads or context to rerank. you can also implement a post-rerank rescoring step that merges model score with business signals. Console can surface those signals in dashboards.
[09:53] Samira: let's talk timeline — when can we kick off?
[09:57] Jordan: if we get the 50k slice and query logs by next Tues we can spin up pilot within 3 business days; two-week run after that.
[10:05] Riley: sounds good. any blockers on compliance docs?
[10:08] Jordan: none; we'll include SOC2, ISO artifact and data processing addendum.
[10:14] Samira: ok thanks. this has been helpful.
[10:18] Jordan: quick recap and next steps coming in chat. thanks everyone.
[10:22] (meeting ends)
